claims.text: This release fundamentally changed how OpenAI sells its models by consolidating its product lineup into one unified model and eliminating the previous distinction between reasoning and non-reasoning products [Source: ev-1].

Specifically, GPT-5 retired separate o-series products (o3, o4-mini, o3-mini, and o3-pro), folding their capabilities into internal "reasoning modes," thereby removing the need for a model picker [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: The new sales approach is characterized by aggressive distribution on the free tier and significantly lower API costs compared to previous generations [Source: ev-1].

While Plus remains at $20/month and Pro at $200/month, API pricing dropped to $1.25 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens for GPT-5, with GPT-5 mini priced even lower at $0.25 / $2 per million tokens [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: This strategy moved the competitive battleground from benchmark demos to "default agency," focusing on models that act rather than just answer [Source: ev-1].
Despite these changes, performance remained strong, with GPT-5 scoring approximately 78.6% on SWE-bench Verified, while achieving these results at a fraction of o-series prices [Source: ev-1].
